beats.beat: The company sells four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM).
It relies on a long-term arrangement with corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited for marketing and distribution – not on its own sales force.
Top 10 customers accounted for around 59% of revenue in each of the last three financial years (FY2015–2017), indicating high customer concentration.
Exports go to only three countries: Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka (total exports of Rs 10.68 crore over five years).

The company lists six competitive strengths: diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, support of holding company, product innovation and R&D, and strong management team.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations (in ₹ crore): FY2013 27.94, FY2014 28.31, FY2015 34.74, FY2016 32.85, FY2017 38.32, H1FY2018 20.60 (annualised ~41.20).
Profit after tax: FY2013 –0.27, FY2014 –0.12, FY2015 1.50, FY2016 0.90, FY2017 1.75, H1FY2018 1.33 (in ₹ crore). The company turned profitable from FY2015 onward.
Net cash from operating activities: FY2013 2.01, FY2014 1.28, FY2015 4.22, FY2016 8.03, FY2017 –3.50, H1FY2018 1.25 (in ₹ crore). Note the negative cash flow in FY2017.

Total assets (in ₹ crore) grew from 27.94 (FY2013) to 34.25 (H1FY2018), while total liabilities (not fully extracted) stood at ₹30.19 crore as of September 30, 2017. Debt details are not fully disclosed in the digest.

beats.beat: Promoters: 20 Microns Limited (corporate promoter), Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, and Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh. They collectively hold 89,48,270 equity shares, i.e., 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.
Promoter group (excluding promoters) holds 21,510 shares, representing 0.24% of pre-issue capital. Pre-issue public holding is nil.
Related-party transactions have occurred in each of the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017, as detailed in the financial statements (Accounting Standard 18).

The company has had instances of non-filing, incorrect filings, or delays in filing statutory forms with the RoC, though these were subsequently filed with additional fees. Certain statutory licences for one manufacturing facility (Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia) have not yet been obtained, creating compliance risk.
The company does not own the premises for two of its manufacturing facilities (Plot 347 GIDC Waghodia, and Plot 104/3 Thenkasi Road, Tirunelveli) nor its administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals segment (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at ~Rs 1,000 billion in FY2017 and grew at 10–12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017.

CRISIL Research projects specialty chemicals to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward, driven by increased consumption, end-use demand, and government initiatives like the Draft National Chemical Policy and 100% FDI allowance.
Within specialty chemicals, sub-segments like construction chemicals, water chemicals, and personal care ingredients are each expected to grow at 15% CAGR over the next 3–5 years.
The industry is highly fragmented, with SMEs holding 70–75% market share; only a few Indian players have the scale to compete with global giants.
India's chemicals imports exceed exports, growing at 6.4% CAGR vs 6% for exports (2012–13 to 2016–17), presenting an import substitution opportunity that the company cites as a strength.
Key regulations include REACH for exports to Europe, GST effective July 2017, and four PCPIRs (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Odisha) with proposed investments of ~Rs 9 trillion.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals, including functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals, and hard minerals.
It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through that company's network.
The company is raising funds through an SME IPO on NSE EMERGE, with the proceeds intended to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility and for general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who this company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares; there is no offer for sale (OFS). The filing does not disclose the exact number of shares or price band (marked as [●]).
Proceeds will be used to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes.
Listing is planned on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE), which enhances visibility and creates a public trading market.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited; the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

offer.heading: The offer
offer.purpose: Explain the IPO structure (fresh issue vs OFS), selling shareholders, use of proceeds, and lead manager

beats.beat: No long-term customer or supplier agreements. All sales are governed by purchase orders, and raw material supply is not contracted, leaving the company exposed to volume and price volatility.
Negative cash flow from operations in FY2017 (Rs -3.50 crore) after positive cash flows in the prior two years, which could strain liquidity if it recurs.
Pending statutory licences and registrations for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, and non-filing instances with RoC expose the company to potential penalties or shutdown.
Product liability claims could arise from defects in products sold domestically or overseas (Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka), potentially harming reputation and finances.
Unsecured loans taken by the company and its promoters are recallable at any time by lenders, creating refinancing risk.

beats.beat: The DRHP does not disclose a peer comparison table, nor does it provide P/E, EPS, NAV, or RoNW for any named competitor. It only describes the industry as highly fragmented with SMEs and global players.

Without a price band or peer multiples, a valuation analysis cannot be performed from the DRHP alone. Investors will need to rely on the post-offer P/E based on the issue price and the company's restated earnings (e.g., EPS of ₹2.43 for FY2017).
